what_it_does: Scientific simulations produce enormous amounts of floating-point data — numbers that represent physical quantities like temperature, pressure, or velocity across a fine-grained spatial grid. Lossless compression shrinks files without discarding any information (unlike image or video compression that trades accuracy for size). The challenge is that existing lossless compressors for floating-point data are either fast or space-efficient, rarely both, and almost none work equally well on both CPUs and GPUs (the separate chips commonly used to accelerate simulation). This paper presents four new compression algorithms that exploit bit-level patterns in the IEEE 754 floating-point number format (the universal standard for how computers represent decimal numbers) — specifically patterns in the exponent (the scale of the number) and mantissa (the significant digits) fields. The algorithms are designed to exploit both CPU-style vector instructions (SIMD) and GPU-style parallel thread execution, and are tested against 18 existing compressors on standard scientific benchmark datasets.
